questions.question: Explain the causes of the Sharpeville and Langa protests of March 1960.
questions.expected_answer: Pass laws: reference book, arrests, fines, endorsement out; hundreds of thousands prosecuted yearly; hated symbol. Sharpeville (near Vereeniging, 1940s township): unemployment, low wages, higher rents, tightened influx control, raids. Western Cape: Coloured Labour Preference Policy, hostels in Langa and Nyanga, raids, threat of removal. PAC anti-pass campaign (Sobukwe): leave passes, present at police stations, "no bail, no defence, no fine", strongest in Vereeniging area and Cape Peninsula; ANC planned 31 March separately.

questions.question: Describe the events at Sharpeville on 21 March 1960 and the Langa march.
questions.expected_answer: Sharpeville: PAC (Nyakane Tsolo) mobilised; crowd about 5 000-7 000 incl. women, children; songs, Izwe Lethu; about 300 police, Saracens, low-flying jets; scuffle at gate after 1 p.m.; police fired without order or warning about 40 seconds; 69 killed (incl. 8 women, 10 children), about 180 wounded, many shot in back; police claimed self-defence; photos (Ian Berry); no prosecutions. Langa: 21 March crowd of about 6 000 baton-charged and fired on, at least 2 killed; strike. Kgosana (23) led about 2 000 on 25 March and about 30 000 on 30 March to Caledon Square; Terblanche promised meeting with Erasmus; crowd sent home peacefully; Kgosana arrested; townships sealed off, strike crushed.

questions.question: Describe the short- and longer-term consequences of Sharpeville and Langa.
questions.expected_answer: Short-term: Luthuli burned pass 26 March; day of mourning 28 March; pass laws suspended 26 March, reintroduced April; state of emergency 30 March, over 11 000 detained; Unlawful Organisations Act, ANC and PAC banned 8 April 1960 (until 1990); capital flight, stock market fall; UN Security Council Resolution 134 (1 April 1960); international condemnation; Verwoerd shot by Pratt 9 April. Longer-term: turn to armed struggle: Umkhonto we Sizwe (Mandela, sabotage from 16 December 1961), Poqo; exile (Tambo); Sobukwe imprisoned, Sobukwe clause until 1969; more repression and detention laws; republic and Commonwealth exit 1961. Memory: UN International Day for Elimination of Racial Discrimination (1966); Human Rights Day 21 March; Mandela signed Constitution at Sharpeville 10 December 1996.
